# Scion 1.0.0 documentation: CLI reference

> Every page below is also at its own URL plus `.md`. Index: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# CLI overview

`dotnet scion` is Scion's command line, a local .NET tool (`Scion.Cli`). Every command has the form
`dotnet scion <noun> <verb>`, prints one JSON envelope outside a terminal (text inside one), always says the
`next_step`, and exits 0, 1, 2 or 3. This page covers installation, the global options (`--format`, `--dry-run`,
`--help`, `--version`), how the CLI finds the project root (`scion.json`), the test build (`--build`, `SCION_BUILD`),
Unity and the editor, the envelope and the exit-code precedence.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion <command> [<verb>] [arguments] [options] [-- player-args]
dotnet scion --help | --version
```

| Command | Verbs | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `doctor` | | [doctor](/scion/cli/doctor/) |
| `init`, `new`, `uninstall` | | [init, new, uninstall](/scion/cli/init/) |
| `build` | `test`, `final` | [build test, build final](/scion/cli/build/) |
| `trial` (alias `trials`) | `list`, `run`, `show`, `approve`, `serve`, `diff`, `eval`, `loop` | [trial run](/scion/cli/trial-run/) and siblings |
| `anchor` | `list`, `show` | [anchor list, anchor show](/scion/cli/anchor/) |
| `graft` | `new`, `check`, `build`, `inject`, `restore`, `disable`, `promote`, `watch` | [graft](/scion/cli/graft/) |
| `bisect` | | [bisect](/scion/cli/bisect/) |
| `diagnose` | | [diagnose](/scion/cli/diagnose/) |
| `index`, `guard` | | [index, guard](/scion/cli/index-and-guard/) |
| `gen` | | [gen](/scion/cli/gen/) |
| `judge` | `list`, `show`, `new`, `vote`, `train`, `run` | [judge](/scion/cli/judge/) |
| `multiverse` | `run`, `show` | [multiverse](/scion/cli/multiverse/) |
| `hunt`, `search` | `run` | [hunt, search](/scion/cli/hunt-and-search/) |
| `mcp` | | [mcp](/scion/cli/mcp/) |

## Description

### Install

```sh
dotnet new tool-manifest            # once per repository, if there is no .config/dotnet-tools.json
dotnet tool install --local Scion.Cli --version 1.0.0
dotnet tool restore                  # on another machine
```

The CLI and the package must have the same version: a DLL injected into a build of another weaver ABI is refused
(SCN131), and `doctor` warns `version_mismatch`.

### How it finds things

| What | Order |
|---|---|
| Project root | The nearest folder upward with `scion.json`. |
| Configuration | `scion.json`, deep-merged with `scion.local.json` (local wins). |
| Test build | `--build <app\|exe\|folder>`, then `SCION_BUILD`, then `scion.local.json`, then `build.test.output.<os>` in `scion.json`. `scion-build.json` must sit next to it. |
| Unity | The version in `ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt`, at the Hub's default path for the OS; `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json` overrides. |
| Editor open | `Temp/UnityLockfile` locked. Builds then go through the open editor (needs `com.unity.pipeline`) or stop with `editor_open`. |
| Ports | A free port per co-op group and per control channel (bind to 0, release). |

### Behavior every command shares

- Commands that write accept `--dry-run` and are idempotent: running one twice changes nothing the second time.
- Output is compact JSON (about 1.5 KB at most): long lists are cut with `"more": N`, and the full data goes to a
  file (`summary.json`) whose path is in the envelope.
- Arguments after `--` go to every player process; a flag also present in `player_args` replaces it.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--format json\|text` | `json` outside a TTY, `text` in one | Output format. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Print what would change; change nothing. |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build to use (commands that run players). |
| `--help`, `-h` | | Help for the command. |
| `--version` | | `1.0.0`. |

## Output

Every command prints one envelope:

<!-- validate: envelope -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":false,"next_step":"run: dotnet scion build test","error":{"code":"build_not_found","message":"no test build at /Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","hint":"run: dotnet scion build test","did_you_mean":[]}}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema_version` | 1. |
| `command` | The command as typed, without options (`trial run`). |
| `ok` | True when the exit code is 0. |
| `next_step` | One line: what to do next. Always present. |
| `warnings[]` | `{code, message}`; never change the exit code. |
| `error` | Only on exit 2 and 3: `code`, `message`, `hint`, `did_you_mean`. |
| command fields | Documented on each command's page and in its JSON Schema. |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | Everything ok (warnings do not count). |
| 1 | A recipe, check, graft check or spec failed. |
| 2 | Usage: unknown command, option or value; nothing matched. |
| 3 | Environment: no build, no Unity, a player crashed, a copy timed out. |

When several copies or steps end differently, the command exits with the highest-priority code: 2, then 3, then 1,
then 0. See [Exit codes](/scion/reference/exit-codes/).

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 2 | No `scion.json` above the current folder. | `dotnet scion init`, or `cd` into the project. |
| `config_invalid` | 3 | `scion.json` does not match its schema. | Fix the key in the message. |
| `unknown_command`, `unknown_option` | 2 | A typo. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build found. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `unity_not_found` | 3 | No Unity of the project's version. | Set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json`. |

Every code: [Error and warning codes](/scion/reference/errors/).

## Examples

### Text output in a script

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --format text
```

### Pick a build for one command

```sh
SCION_BUILD=/tmp/orchard-test/Orchard.app dotnet scion trial list
```

## See also

- [Install](/scion/start/install/)
- [Reading results](/scion/agents/reading-results/)
- [Exit codes](/scion/reference/exit-codes/)
- [Error and warning codes](/scion/reference/errors/)
- [Configuration](/scion/reference/configuration/)

# doctor

`dotnet scion doctor` checks that everything Scion needs is in place and says what to do about anything that is not.
It reports one check per line with a `hint`, the suggested number of parallel copies for this machine, the
project's adoption level (`adoption_level`, 1 to 3) and the next step to the next level (`adoption_next`).
`--level` sets how deep the checks go.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion doctor [--level 1|2|3] [--format json|text]
```

## Description

| Level | Checks |
|---|---|
| 1 (default) | `scion.json` and `ScionSettings.json` parse; CLI and package versions match; .NET SDK; Unity of the project's version; the editor lock. |
| 2 | Level 1, plus: the test build exists, has `SCION_TRIALS`, is not stale; `scion-build.json` reads; the output folder is writable; free memory and cores. |
| 3 | Level 2, plus: starts the test build with `-scion-list` (recipes, adapters, SCN201 to SCN203); the judge's eye model; Git LFS for baselines; suppressions with justifications. |

Each check has an `id`, a `status` (`ok`, `warn`, `fail`), a `detail` and, unless ok, a `hint`.

`suggested_copies` is the smaller of (cores - 1) and (free memory / memory per copy), using the last run's
measurement or 600 MB.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--level 1\|2\|3` | 1 | Check depth (not the adoption level). |
| `--format json\|text` | auto | Output format. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/doctor -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"doctor","ok":true,"level":2,"version":"1.0.0","adoption_level":2,"adoption_next":"level 3: register an ISimulation over Orchard.Core (see Core API)","checks":[{"id":"config","status":"ok","detail":"/Users/alex/orchard/scion.json"},{"id":"versions","status":"ok","detail":"CLI 1.0.0, package 1.0.0"},{"id":"unity","status":"ok","detail":"6000.3.25f1"},{"id":"build","status":"ok","detail":".scion/builds/test/Orchard.app (4c49a1e0b2f3)"},{"id":"machine","status":"ok","detail":"10 cores, 9.1 GB free of 16.0 GB"}],"suggested_copies":6,"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run -j 6"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level` | The check depth that ran. |
| `version` | The CLI version. |
| `adoption_level` | 1 grafts, 2 trials, 3 multiverse. |
| `adoption_next` | What is missing for the next level, or null at 3. |
| `checks[]` | `id`, `status`, `detail`, `hint`. |
| `suggested_copies` | For `trial run -j`. |

Schema: `https://jand-s.github.io/scion/schemas/v1/cli/doctor.schema.json`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | No check failed (warnings allowed). |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | A check failed. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 2 | No `scion.json`. | `dotnet scion init`. |
| warning `version_mismatch` | 0 | The CLI and the package differ. | Install the same version of both. |
| warning `build_stale` | 0 | The test build is older than the sources. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning `low_memory` | 0 | Not enough free memory for 2 copies. | Close apps or run `-j 1`. |
| `model_missing` | 3 | Level 3: the judge's eye model is not downloaded. | Run the command in `hint`. |

## Examples

### The deepest check

```sh
dotnet scion doctor --level 3
```

### Only the failing checks, in a script

```sh
dotnet scion doctor --format json | jq '.checks[] | select(.status != "ok")'
```

## See also

- [Install](/scion/start/install/)
- [Parallel copies](/scion/trials/parallel/)
- [Find non-determinism](/scion/determinism/diagnose/)

# init, new, uninstall

Three commands manage Scion in a project. `dotnet scion init` adds Scion to an existing Unity project (`scion.json`,
`ScionSettings.json`, the grafts folder and `.asmref`, `.gitignore` entries, the agent integration). `dotnet scion
new` creates a whole project from a genre template, or scaffolds a feature, effect, graft or trial inside one.
`dotnet scion uninstall` removes what `init` added. All three accept `--dry-run` and report `created`, `changed`,
`removed` and `skipped` files.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion init [--existing] [--agent claude|codex|cursor|none] [--game-assembly <name>] [--grafts-folder <path>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion new --genre tactics|action|platformer|blank --name <Name> [--players 1-4] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion new feature|effect|graft|trial <Name> [--after|--before <Type.Method>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion uninstall [--purge] [--dry-run]
```

## Description

`init` never overwrites: an existing file is listed in `skipped`. `uninstall` reverses `init` and keeps your grafts,
recipes and baselines unless `--purge`.

## init

| Creates or changes | Content |
|---|---|
| `scion.json` | Paths, defaults and builds for this project. |
| `ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json` | `build.main_assembly`, analyzer scope. |
| `Assets/<Game>/Grafts/<Game>.Grafts.asmref` | Points the grafts folder at the game assembly. |
| `Packages/manifest.json` | Adds `me.jandson.scion` if missing. |
| `.config/dotnet-tools.json` | Adds `Scion.Cli`. |
| `.gitignore` | `.scion/`, `scion.local.json`, `Library/Scion/`. |
| `.gitattributes` | LFS for `scion/baselines/**/*.png`. |
| agent files | With `--agent claude`: the plugin's hooks in `.claude/settings.json` and `CLAUDE.md` pointing to the index. |

`--existing` is required when the project already has scripts: `init` then asks (or takes `--game-assembly`) which
assembly is the game.

## new

| Form | Creates |
|---|---|
| `new --genre tactics --name Orchard --players 4` | A Unity project at level 3: core with `ISimulation`, presentation, grafts, adapter, recipes, specs, tests, exemplars. |
| `new feature <Name>` | A `RuleModifier<T>`, its data row, a recipe and a completeness entry. |
| `new effect <Name>` | An enum case, its strategy, a cue, a completeness entry. |
| `new graft <Name> --after <Type.Method>` | A promoted graft with the right signature (drafts use `graft new`). |
| `new trial <Name>` | A recipe for the project's adapter, with checks. |

Genres: `tactics` (turn-based, grid), `action` (real time), `platformer`, `blank` (only the layers).

## uninstall

Removes `scion.json`, `ScionSettings.json`, the `.asmref`, the package and tool entries and the agent files. With
`--purge`, also `scion/` (drafts, recipes, presets, baselines, judge data) and `.scion/`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--existing` | init | Adopt a project with scripts. |
| `--agent <name>` | init | Agent integration: `claude` (default), `codex`, `cursor`, `none`. |
| `--game-assembly <name>` | init | The game assembly, without asking. |
| `--grafts-folder <path>` | init | Default `Assets/<Game>/Grafts`. |
| `--genre`, `--name`, `--players` | new | Project template. |
| `--after`, `--before` | new graft | The target. |
| `--purge` | uninstall | Also delete Scion data. |
| `--dry-run` | all | Change nothing. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/init -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"init","ok":true,"dry_run":false,"created":["scion.json","ProjectSettings/ScionSettings.json","Assets/Orchard/Grafts/Orchard.Grafts.asmref"],"changed":["Packages/manifest.json",".gitignore",".gitattributes",".config/dotnet-tools.json"],"skipped":[],"adoption_level":1,"next_step":"dotnet scion doctor"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done (or nothing to do). |
| 2 | Bad option, or `init` without `--existing` in a project with scripts. |
| 3 | A file could not be written. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | `init` in a project with scripts and no `--existing`. | Add `--existing`. |
| `config_invalid` | 3 | An existing `scion.json` is invalid. | Fix it; `init` never overwrites. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | Unknown genre or kind. | Use one of the listed values. |

## Examples

### Preview init in an existing project

```sh
dotnet scion init --existing --game-assembly Orchard.Runtime --dry-run
```

### A four-player tactics project

```sh
dotnet scion new --genre tactics --name Orchard --players 4
```

## See also

- [Start a new project](/scion/start/new-project/)
- [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/start/existing-project/)
- [Enforcement](/scion/standard/enforcement/)

# build test, build final

`dotnet scion build test` builds the test player (Mono, `SCION_SLOTS` and `SCION_TRIALS`) and writes
`scion-build.json` next to it; `dotnet scion build final` builds the shipping player without test defines. The CLI
runs Unity in batchmode with `build.test.method` or `build.final.method` from `scion.json`, or, when the editor is
open and `com.unity.pipeline` is installed, builds through the open editor. Compile errors come back with file,
line and code.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion build test  [--out <dir>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion build final [--out <dir>] [--dry-run]
```

## Description

1. Finds Unity and checks the editor lock.
2. Closed editor: runs `Unity -batchmode -quit -projectPath <unity_project> -executeMethod <method> -scion-build-out <dir>`.
   Open editor with the pipeline package: writes `Temp/Scion/ScionBuildEntry.cs` and runs it in the editor.
3. Reads the `BUILD_RESULT` line and the log, and collects compile errors and SCN diagnostics.
4. On success, reads `scion-build.json` and prints the build id.

The output folder defaults to `build.test.output.<os>` (or `build.final.output.<os>`) in `scion.json`.

## build test

Builds with `ScionBuild.TestFromCommandLine` (or the method in `build.test.method`): Mono backend, `SCION_SLOTS` and
`SCION_TRIALS` added for the build only, `scion-build.json` written with the slots and recipe names. Trials, warm
copies, injection and the multiverse mosaic all need this build.

## build final

Builds with `ScionBuild.FinalFromCommandLine` (or `build.final.method`): the project's backend (IL2CPP by default),
no test defines, grafts called directly. It fails with SCN121 if a test define is set anywhere in the build.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--out <dir>` | from `scion.json` | Output folder. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Print the program and arguments; build nothing. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/build -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"build test","ok":false,"channel":"batchmode","seconds":21.4,"log":".scion/logs/build-20261012-130000.log","build_id":null,"output":".scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","errors":[{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Grafts/CritShake.cs","line":18,"code":"SCN104","message":"The signature of CritShake.After does not match HitPresenter.Play.","hint":"Expected: public static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c)","did_you_mean":[]}],"errors_total":1,"next_step":"fix Assets/Orchard/Grafts/CritShake.cs:18, then: dotnet scion build test"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `channel` | `batchmode` or `editor`. |
| `seconds` | Build time. |
| `build_id` | 12 hex, or null on failure. |
| `output` | The player path. |
| `errors[]` | `file`, `line`, `code` (`CS0103`, `SCN104`...), `message`, `hint`. |
| `errors_total` | All errors, when the list is cut. |
| `program`, `args` | With `--dry-run`. |

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Built. |
| 1 | Compile errors or a build guard (SCN120, SCN121). |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | No Unity, editor open without the pipeline, Unity crashed. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `editor_open` | 3 | The editor is open and `com.unity.pipeline` is missing. | Close the editor, or install the pipeline package. |
| `unity_not_found` | 3 | No Unity of the project's version. | Set `unity.editor` in `scion.local.json`. |
| `unity_failed` | 3 | Unity exited without a `BUILD_RESULT` line. | Read the log in `log`. |
| warning `unity_exit` | 0 | Unity exited non-zero after a successful build. | Usually harmless; read the log. |
| `SCN120`, `SCN121` | 1 | Build guards. | See [Build modes](/scion/grafts/build-modes/). |

## Examples

### Show the Unity command

```sh
dotnet scion build test --dry-run
```

### A final build for a store

```sh
dotnet scion build final --out /tmp/orchard-release
```

## See also

- [Build modes](/scion/grafts/build-modes/)
- [scion-build.json](/scion/reference/files/scion-build-json/)
- [Editor API](/scion/reference/api/editor/)

# trial list

`dotnet scion trial list` lists the recipes a run can play. By default it reads recipe names from the test build's
assemblies (without starting it) and adds the sources in `scion/recipes/` and the captured and found matches. With
`--ids` it starts the build with `-scion-list` and prints every expanded id (variants, modes, seeds) with players,
tags and flags.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial list [patterns] [--ids] [--tag <tags>] [--players <n>] [--build <path>]
```

## Description

| Source | `source` | Read how |
|---|---|---|
| The test build | `build` | Recipe classes found in `Managed/*.dll` without running the player. |
| `scion/recipes/*.cs` | `staging` | Recipe sources compiled with `--recipes`. |
| `scion/recipes/captured/*.match.json` | `captured` | One `CapturedMatch` id per file. |
| `scion/recipes/found/*.match.json` | `found` | Finds of the hunter. |

A recipe that cannot be built (no public parameterless constructor) is listed with `problem`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `patterns` | all | Names, ids or globs. |
| `--ids` | off | Expand ids by starting the player with `-scion-list`. |
| `--tag <tags>` | | Only recipes with one of the tags (needs `--ids`). |
| `--players <n>` | | Only recipes with that `Players` (needs `--ids`). |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-list -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial list","ok":true,"build":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/builds/test/Orchard.app","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","count":7,"recipes":[{"name":"SlashHit","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"FireballArea","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"KnightFalls","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"CoopTurn","source":"build","players":4},{"name":"HudStates","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"UnitGallery","source":"build","players":1},{"name":"CapturedMatch","id":"CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]","source":"captured","players":1}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run"}
```

With `--ids`, each entry has `id`, `type`, `tags` and `explicit`, and the full list is in `recipes.json` of a
temporary folder.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Listed. |
| 2 | A pattern matched nothing. |
| 3 | No build, or the player failed with `--ids`. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No recipe matches. | Use `did_you_mean`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning `recipe_unbuildable` | 0 | A recipe has no public parameterless constructor (SCN201). | Add one. |
| warning `unreadable_dll` | 0 | A DLL of the build could not be read. | Rebuild. |

## Examples

### Every id of one recipe

```sh
dotnet scion trial list SlashHit --ids
```

### Only co-op recipes

```sh
dotnet scion trial list --ids --players 4
```

## See also

- [Write a recipe](/scion/trials/recipes/)
- [Variants, modes and seeds](/scion/trials/variants/)
- [recipes.json](/scion/reference/files/recipes-json/)

# trial run

`dotnet scion trial run` is the command you use most. It selects recipes, starts copies of the test build (or uses
warm copies), splits the work into shards and co-op groups, waits, compares every result with `scion/baselines/`,
writes `summary.json`, `summary.tsv` and `compare.json` in a new run folder, and prints a short envelope with counts,
failures, changes, determinism and the `next_step`. It also runs specs, variants, the mosaic and the motion pack.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial run [patterns] [-j N] [--rounds N] [selection options] [capture options]
                       [--grafts <dll>] [--recipes <dll>] [--warm] [--spec <Name>] [--variants a,b]
                       [--build <path>] [-- player-args]
```

## Description

1. Selects ids: patterns, `--tag`, `--players`, `--mode`, `--seeds`, `--changed`, `--failed`; `Explicit` recipes only
   when named.
2. Creates `<trials.out>/<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>/` and deletes runs beyond `keep_runs`.
3. Starts copies (cold) or sends `run` to warm copies (`--warm`). Co-op recipes run in groups of `Players` copies.
4. Waits, with `--timeout` per copy and the 120 s watchdog.
5. Compares each (id, round) with its baseline: hash, frames, images (cold runs only), rule digest.
6. Writes `summary.json` (the full envelope plus `copies[]`), `summary.tsv`, `compare.json`, `diff/` heatmaps.
7. Prints the envelope, with lists cut to stay short.

## Options

### Selection

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `patterns` | every non-`Explicit` recipe | Names, ids or globs, comma- or space-separated. |
| `--tag <tags>` | | Recipes with any of the tags. |
| `--players <n>` | all | Recipes with that `Players`. |
| `--mode <name>` | none | One mode of `[assembly: TrialModes]`. |
| `--seeds <a-b>` | none | Repeat each id per seed; ids get `#<seed>`. |
| `--changed` | | The ids that were `changed` or `stale` in the last run. |
| `--failed` | | The ids that failed in the last run. |

### Execution

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-j N` | `trials.defaults.copies` | Parallel copies. |
| `--rounds N` | 1 | Rounds per id. |
| `--seed N` | 1 | Run seed (`RunSeed`). |
| `--timeout <s>` | 300 | Real seconds per copy. |
| `--check` | off | Frame-by-frame determinism report (`determinism.tsv`). |
| `--jitter <ms>` | 0 | Random real-time sleep per frame from the second round. |
| `--warm` | off | Use warm copies (`trial serve`); compares hash and frames only. |
| `--mosaic <K>` | off | K arenas per process. |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build. |

### Capture

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--window` | headless | Render to a window. |
| `--size WxH` | `trials.defaults.size` | Capture size. |
| `--frames` | off | Every frame as PNG. |
| `--raw` | off | Keep raw frames. |
| `--sound` | muted | Audio on. |
| `--motion` | off | The motion pack. |
| `--learn-unstable <n>` | off | Run n extra times and learn the unstable mask (cap 2 %). |

### Code and values

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--grafts <dll>` | none | Inject a draft graft DLL at startup (`-scion-inject`); the run cannot be approved. |
| `--recipes <dll>` | none | Load recipes from a DLL; same `Name` replaces. Repeatable. |
| `--set <key>=<value>` | none | Override a tunable (`tunable:CritShake.Strength=0.8`). Repeatable. |
| `--preset <name\|blend>` | none | Apply a preset or blend to every id. |
| `--variants a,b,c` | none | One variant per preset or blend; ids get `[preset=<name>]`. |
| `--spec <Name>` | none | Run a spec; the envelope gets `spec`. |
| `-- args` | | Passed to every player; replaces the same flag in `player_args`. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial run","ok":false,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","build_id":"4c49a1e0b2f3","copies":6,"wall_s":27.1,"runs":{"recipes":6,"rounds":2,"total":12,"ok":11,"failed":1,"changed":1,"within":0,"px_changed":0,"new":0,"stale":0},"failed":[{"id":"KnightFalls","round":1,"copy":3,"error":"timeout (30s): unit down animation","report":"q3/KnightFalls/r1/report.md"}],"changed":[{"id":"SlashHit","vs_approved":"changed","hash":"same","image":"q0/SlashHit/r1/window.png","diff":"diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}],"determinism":{"hash_stable":true,"frame_jitter":[]},"next_step":"read q3/KnightFalls/r1/report.md; SlashHit changed only in images: see diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `run` | The run folder; paths in the envelope are relative to it. |
| `copies` | Processes started (or warm copies used). |
| `runs` | Counts: ids, rounds, (id, round) pairs, ok, failed, and per verdict. |
| `failed[]` | `id`, `round`, `copy`, `error`, `report`. |
| `changed[]` | `id`, `vs_approved`, `hash` (`same`/`changed`), `image`, `diff`. |
| `determinism` | `hash_stable`, `frame_jitter`. |
| `mosaic` | K, when used. |
| `spec` | With `--spec`: `name`, `ok`, `variants[]`, `verdict`. |

Files: [summary.json, summary.tsv, compare.json](/scion/reference/files/summary/).

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Every recipe passed. Verdicts such as `changed` do not fail a run. |
| 1 | A recipe or check failed, or a spec failed. |
| 2 | Bad option or a pattern matched nothing. |
| 3 | No build, a copy crashed or timed out, environment errors. |

Copies are combined with precedence 2 > 3 > 1 > 0.

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No id matches. | `did_you_mean`; `trial list --ids`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `build_wrong_mode` | 3 | The build lacks `SCION_TRIALS`. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| `player_crashed` | 3 | A copy exited without outputs. | Read `q<i>/player.log`. |
| `copy_timeout` | 3 | A copy passed `--timeout` or was interrupted. | Raise `--timeout`, or find the stuck `WaitUntil`. |
| `no_free_port` | 3 | No free port for a group. | Close other servers. |
| `no_copies` | 3 | `--warm` with no warm copies. | `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`. |
| `mosaic_unsupported` | 3 | `--mosaic` and no `IMosaicAdapter`. | Implement it or drop `--mosaic`. |
| warning `build_stale` | 0 | Sources changed after the build. | Rebuild before trusting the result. |
| warning `px_unstable` | 0 | Pixels vary between rounds. | See [Verify determinism](/scion/determinism/verify/). |
| warning `shard_ignored` | 0 | `-scion-shard` passed after `--`. | Let the CLI shard. |

## Examples

### The everyday run

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2
```

### Combat only, with the motion pack, at 720p

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --tag combat --motion --size 1280x720
```

### A draft graft against every recipe

```sh
dotnet scion trial run --grafts .scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
```

## See also

- [How trials work](/scion/trials/overview/)
- [Parallel copies](/scion/trials/parallel/)
- [summary.json, summary.tsv, compare.json](/scion/reference/files/summary/)
- [Reading results](/scion/agents/reading-results/)
- [Player command line](/scion/reference/player-flags/)

# trial show

`dotnet scion trial show` reads a run folder and prints the essentials for some ids: rounds ok and failed, hashes,
frame counts, the verdict against the baseline with its reasons, and the **paths** of `report.md` and the images.
It never prints image content: open the paths. With `--grid` it writes baseline, current and difference side by side.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial show <Id...> | --failed | --changed [--run <run>] [--image window|context|still|sheet|motion-diff] [--grid]
```

## Description

Defaults to the last run. For each id it merges every round and copy. `--image` limits `images[]` to one kind. `--grid`
writes `diff/<IdDir>/r<n>/<artifact>.grid.png` (baseline, current, heatmap in three columns) and returns its path.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id...>` | | Ids or patterns. |
| `--failed` | | Ids with a failed round. |
| `--changed` | | Ids with verdict `changed`, `stale`, `within` or `px_changed`. |
| `--run <run>` | last run | A run folder name or path. |
| `--image <kind>` | all | Only that image kind. |
| `--grid` | off | Write and return comparison grids. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-show -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial show","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","count":1,"recipes":[{"id":"KnightFalls","rounds":{"ok":1,"failed":1},"hashes":["1B44E07AC9D20F13"],"frames":[52],"vs_approved":"same","round":1,"copy":3,"report":"q3/KnightFalls/r1/report.md","images":["q3/KnightFalls/r1/window.png","q3/KnightFalls/r1/context.png"],"failed":[{"round":1,"copy":3,"error":"timeout (30s): unit down animation"}]}],"next_step":"read q3/KnightFalls/r1/report.md"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `recipes[].rounds` | `ok` and `failed` counts. |
| `hashes`, `frames` | Distinct values seen across rounds. |
| `vs_approved`, `reasons`, `stale` | Verdict and why. |
| `px_diff` | Fraction of frames whose pixel hash differs from the baseline. |
| `report`, `images` | Paths relative to the run. |
| `grid` | With `--grid`. |

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Shown. |
| 2 | No such id or run. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | The id is not in the run. | `did_you_mean`. |
| warning `result_unreadable` | 0 | A `result.json` is missing or broken. | The copy crashed; read its `player.log`. |
| warning `summary_not_written` | 0 | The run was interrupted before `summary.json`. | Run again. |

## Examples

### Everything that failed

```sh
dotnet scion trial show --failed
```

### A grid for review

```sh
dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid --image window
```

## See also

- [Reading results](/scion/agents/reading-results/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/trials/baselines/)
- [Image comparison](/scion/trials/image-comparison/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial approve

`dotnet scion trial approve` writes the results of a run into `scion/baselines/` as the new approved state and stages
the files with `git add` (it never commits). A reason is required. Approving ids that already have a baseline needs a
person at an interactive terminal; agents get `human_required`. Approval is all or nothing.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial approve <Id...> | --changed | --new --reason "<text>" [--run <run>] [--dry-run]
```

## Description

For each selected id, from the given run (default: last):

1. Refuses if any round failed, the run used `--grafts` or `--warm`, or rounds disagree on the hash.
2. Checks who is approving: without a TTY, only `new` ids pass; anything else is `human_required`.
3. With a TTY and non-`new` ids, shows the list and asks for confirmation.
4. Writes `baseline.json` (hash, frames, fps, player args, rule digest, approval) and this platform's folder
   (`platform.json`, `frames.tsv`, images, learned mask).
5. Runs `git add` on the written files.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id...>` | | Ids or patterns. |
| `--changed` | | Every id whose verdict is not `same` or `new`. |
| `--new` | | Every `new` id. |
| `--reason "<text>"` | required | Why; stored in the baseline. |
| `--run <run>` | last run | The run to approve from. |
| `--dry-run` | off | List what would be approved. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-approve -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial approve","ok":false,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-143200","approved":0,"unchanged":0,"baselines":[],"staged":false,"refused":[{"id":"SlashHit","why":"changed needs a person at a terminal"}],"needs_person":true,"next_step":"ask a person to run: dotnet scion trial approve SlashHit --reason \"crit shake is stronger\"","error":{"code":"human_required","message":"approving changed baselines needs an interactive terminal","hint":"show the person trial show SlashHit --grid and the command in next_step","did_you_mean":[]}}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `approved`, `unchanged` | Ids written; ids already equal to the baseline. |
| `baselines[]` | `id`, `was` (the verdict), `round`, `copy`, `dir`. |
| `staged` | `git add` succeeded. |
| `refused[]` | `id`, `why`. |
| `needs_person` | True when a person must run the command. |
| `would_approve` | With `--dry-run`. |

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Approved (or nothing to approve). |
| 1 | Refused: a failed round, `--grafts`, `--warm`, unstable hash. |
| 2 | `human_required`, missing `--reason`, no match. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `human_required` | 2 | Non-`new` ids without a TTY. | Stop; give the person the command. |
| `refused` | 1 | An id cannot be approved. | Read `refused[].why`. |
| `usage` | 2 | No `--reason`. | Add one. |
| warning `not_staged` | 0 | `git add` failed. | Stage by hand; check Git LFS. |
| warning `baseline_unreadable` | 0 | An old baseline could not be read; it is replaced. | Review the diff in git. |

## Examples

### Agents: approve the first baselines

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve --new --reason "baselines for the new gallery"
```

### People: approve a reviewed change

```sh
dotnet scion trial approve SlashHit --reason "crit shake is stronger"
```

## See also

- [Baselines and approval](/scion/trials/baselines/)
- [Hooks](/scion/agents/hooks/)
- [baseline.json and platform.json](/scion/reference/files/baselines/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial serve

`dotnet scion trial serve -j N` starts N warm copies of the test build in the background: each prepares every
adapter and waits idle on a local control channel. `trial run --warm` and `graft inject` use them. Without `-j`, the
command lists the live copies; `--stop` ends them.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial serve [-j N] [--stop] [--window] [--build <path>]
```

## Description

Each copy starts with `-scion-trials -scion-serve -scion-control 0 -scion-out .scion/serve/q<i>` (no `-scion-quit`),
writes `control.json` and `~/.scion/live/<pid>.json`, and reaches `idle`. The command returns when all are idle. If
copies of the same build are already live, `-j N` starts only the missing ones.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `-j N` | none (list only) | Copies to have running. |
| `--stop` | | Send `quit` to every live copy of this build. |
| `--window` | headless | Windows for the copies. |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-serve -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial serve","ok":true,"copies":[{"q":0,"pid":4242,"port":51234,"state":"idle","out":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/serve/q0"},{"q":1,"pid":4243,"port":51240,"state":"running","out":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/serve/q1"}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run --warm"}
```

With `--stop`: `{"stopped": 2}`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Copies idle, listed or stopped. |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | A copy failed to start or prepare. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prepare_failed` | 3 | An adapter's `Prepare` failed in a copy. | Read `.scion/serve/q<i>/player.log`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning `build_changed` | 0 | Live copies run an older build. | `trial serve --stop`, then serve again. |
| warning `recycle` | 0 | A copy passed 50 injections and is being restarted. | Nothing; it comes back idle. |

## Examples

### Two warm copies

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve -j 2
```

### Stop them

```sh
dotnet scion trial serve --stop
```

## See also

- [Warm copies](/scion/trials/warm-copies/)
- [Control protocol](/scion/reference/control-protocol/)
- [Live injection](/scion/grafts/injection/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial diff

`dotnet scion trial diff` compares two run folders (or two copies inside runs) without baselines: for each id in
both, whether the hash is the same, the frame counts, the first frame where the per-frame data differs and its cause,
and an image comparison with a heatmap per artifact. Use it for before and after a graft, or two presets.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial diff <runA> <runB> [Id...]
```

## Description

`runA` and `runB` are run folder names, paths, or `<run>/q<i>` for one copy. Ids default to every id present in
both. Frame data is compared column by column in the cause order of `determinism.tsv` (`state`, `tick`, `rng`,
`unscaled`, `time`, `px`, `frames`). Images use each id's tolerance and masks; heatmaps go to
`<runB>/diff/<IdDir>/r<n>/<artifact>.diff.png`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<runA> <runB>` | required | The two sides. |
| `Id...` | common ids | Limit to these. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-diff -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial diff","ok":true,"a":"20261011-143200","b":"20261011-150512","recipes":[{"id":"SlashHit","hash":"same","frames":[46,46],"first_frame":14,"cause":"px","images":[{"file":"window.png","status":"changed","ratio":0.021,"diff":"diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}]},{"id":"KnightFalls","hash":"same","frames":[52,52],"first_frame":null,"cause":null,"images":[{"file":"window.png","status":"same","ratio":0,"diff":null}]}],"next_step":"look at diff/SlashHit/r1/window.diff.png"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Compared (differences do not fail). |
| 2 | A run or id not found. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No such run or id. | Use the folder names under `trials.out`. |
| warning `pairs_missing` | 0 | Some ids exist in only one run. | Listed in `warnings`; select common ids. |

## Examples

### Before and after a graft

```sh
dotnet scion trial diff 20261011-143200 20261011-143512 SlashHit FireballArea
```

### Two copies of one run

```sh
dotnet scion trial diff 20261011-143200/q0 20261011-143200/q3 KnightFalls
```

## See also

- [A/B comparisons](/scion/evaluation/ab-comparison/)
- [Image comparison](/scion/trials/image-comparison/)
- [Verify determinism](/scion/determinism/verify/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial eval

`dotnet scion trial eval` sends the images of a run to the evaluators configured in `scion.json` and collects their
scores. It writes `eval-in.json` with blind items, runs `process` evaluators, or waits for an `eval-out.json` you
import (agents), and writes `evals.tsv`. Scores never change an exit code or a verdict.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial eval <run> --with <a,b> [--questions <file>] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion trial eval <run> --import <eval-out.json>
```

## Description

1. Collects the run's ids and their `window.png`, `context.png`, stills and `metrics.json`.
2. Shuffles them under blind labels and writes `<run>/eval-in.json` with the questions (default: the questions of the
   judge heads in `judge.dir`).
3. For each `process` evaluator: runs its `command` with the two file paths and reads `eval-out.json`.
4. For `agent` evaluators: stops, with `next_step` telling the agent to answer the file and import it.
5. Maps labels back to ids and writes `evals.tsv` and the `eval` column of `summary.tsv`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<run>` | required | The run folder. |
| `--with a,b` | | Evaluators by name. |
| `--questions <file>` | judge questions | A question file. |
| `--import <file>` | | Import an answer file. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Write `eval-in.json` only. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-eval -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial eval","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/runs/20261011-150512","evaluators":["agent"],"items":3,"exported":"eval-in.json","imported":null,"evals":"evals.tsv","next_step":"answer eval-in.json into eval-out.json, then: dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --import eval-out.json"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Exported, scored or imported. |
| 1 | A process evaluator failed. |
| 2 | Unknown evaluator, bad answer file. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | Evaluator not in `scion.json`. | `did_you_mean`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `eval-out.json` does not validate. | Check it against `judge-answer.schema.json`. |
| `not_supported` | 2 | An evaluator with `gate: true`. | Scores never gate; write an `ITrialCheck`. |

## Examples

### A script evaluator

```sh
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with contrast-script
```

### Agent round trip

```sh
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with agent
dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --import eval-out.json
```

## See also

- [Evaluators](/scion/evaluation/evaluators/)
- [eval-in.json, eval-out.json, evals.tsv](/scion/reference/files/evals/)
- [Questions and answers](/scion/judge/questions/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# trial loop

`dotnet scion trial loop` plays one id over and over in a test build: the whole recipe, or a span of turns of a
captured match. Each pass restores the saved start state and replays; injections made between passes apply on the
next one. It is the engine of the live loop.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion trial loop <Id> [--from <file>] [--span a..b] [--passes N] [--window] [--build <path>]
```

## Description

1. Starts one copy with a control channel (`-scion-control 0`), and `-scion-match <file>` when the id is a match.
2. Plays to the start of `--span` once and saves the state (`ISaveable`); without `--span`, the recipe start.
3. Loops: restore, play the span, write `pass<N>/`, apply pending injections, repeat.
4. Stops on Ctrl-C, after `--passes`, or when a pass changes the hash (an injected graft touched rules).

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id>` | required | A recipe id, usually `CapturedMatch[match=<name>]`. |
| `--from <file>` | | A `.match.json` or `telemetry.jsonl` to take the window from. |
| `--span a..b` | whole recipe | Turns to loop, inclusive. |
| `--passes N` | until stopped | Number of passes. |
| `--window` | headless | Show the window. |
| `--build <path>` | discovery | The test build. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/trial-loop -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"trial loop","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/loops/20261012-103000","id":"SlashHit","span":null,"passes":3,"injects":1,"last":{"ok":true,"hash":"9F3A0C11D2E4B5A6","frames":46,"window":"pass3/window.png"},"stopped_by":"passes","next_step":"compare passes: dotnet scion trial diff 20261012-103000/pass1 20261012-103000/pass3"}
```

`stopped_by` is `passes`, `stop`, `interrupt` or `error`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Stopped by passes, stop or interrupt. |
| 1 | A pass failed or changed the hash. |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | The copy failed, or the state cannot be saved. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `not_forkable` | 3 | `--span` needs `ISaveable`. | Implement it, or loop the whole recipe. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | `--span` outside the match. | Check `turns`. |
| `interrupted` | 0 | Ctrl-C. | Normal stop. |

## Examples

### Two turns of a match, in a window

```sh
dotnet scion trial loop "CapturedMatch[match=knight-dies-to-crit]" --span 3..4 --window
```

### Five passes headless

```sh
dotnet scion trial loop SlashHit --passes 5
```

## See also

- [The live loop](/scion/explore/live-loop/)
- [graft](/scion/cli/graft/)
- [Turn any match into a recipe](/scion/trials/captured-matches/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# anchor list, anchor show

`dotnet scion anchor list` reads the test build with Mono.Cecil (without starting it) and lists every method that can
be an anchor: its slot id, its `[Anchor]` id and doc, whether it has a slot in this build, and the promoted grafts on
it. `dotnet scion anchor show <id>` prints one anchor: the signature, the grafts in run order and a graft declaration
that binds to it.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion anchor list [--search <text>] [--type <Type>] [--build <path>]
dotnet scion anchor show <id> [--build <path>]
```

## Description

Eligibility follows the weaver's rules ([Anchors](/scion/grafts/anchors/)): methods that cannot be anchors are left
out. Each eligible method appears twice, once per side (`B__` before, `A__` after).

## anchor list

Lists anchors, sorted by type and method. `--search` matches the type, method, `[Anchor]` id or doc
(case-insensitive); `--type` limits to one type's full name.

## anchor show

`<id>` is an `[Anchor]` id (`presentation.hit`), a slot id (`A__...`) or `Type.Method`. The output has `example`: a
complete graft method that compiles against the anchor, with `ref Call<T>` when the target returns a value.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--search <text>` | list | Filter by text. |
| `--type <Type>` | list | One type. |
| `--build <path>` | both | The test build. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/anchor-show -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"anchor show","ok":true,"anchor":{"id":"A__Orchard_Presentation_HitPresenter__Play__HitEvent","anchor":"presentation.hit","target":"Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play","signature":"float Play(HitEvent e)","slot":true,"doc":"Plays one hit and returns how long it lasts.","grafts":[{"name":"Orchard.Grafts.HitFlash.After","kind":"after","priority":0,"observe":false,"promoted":true}],"example":"[After(typeof(HitPresenter), nameof(HitPresenter.Play))]\npublic static void After(HitPresenter presenter, HitEvent e, ref Call<float> c) { }"},"next_step":"dotnet scion graft new MyGraft --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play"}
```

`anchor list` returns `total` and `anchors[]` with `id`, `anchor`, `target`, `signature`, `slot`, `doc` and
`promoted` ([Anchors](/scion/grafts/anchors/) has an example).

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Listed or shown. |
| 2 | No anchor with that id. |
| 3 | No build. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | No anchor matches. | `did_you_mean`; `anchor list --search`. |
| `build_not_found` | 3 | No test build. | `dotnet scion build test`. |
| warning `name_at_run_time` | 0 | A graft names its target with a string built at run time; it cannot be listed. | Use `nameof` or a literal. |

## Examples

### Every camera anchor

```sh
dotnet scion anchor list --type Orchard.Presentation.CameraRig
```

### Show by method name

```sh
dotnet scion anchor show Orchard.Presentation.Hud.ShowTurn
```

## See also

- [Anchors](/scion/grafts/anchors/)
- [graft](/scion/cli/graft/)
- [Grafts API](/scion/reference/api/grafts/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# graft

The `graft` commands cover a graft's whole life outside Unity: `graft new` writes a draft with the right signature,
`graft check` runs Roslyn and the weaver rules against the test build, `graft build` compiles drafts into a DLL,
`graft inject`, `graft restore` and `graft disable` change running copies, `graft promote` moves a draft into the
game, and `graft watch` repeats build, inject and run on every save.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion graft new <Name> --after|--before <Type.Method> [--dry-run]
dotnet scion graft check [files] [--strict] [--hook]
dotnet scion graft build [files]
dotnet scion graft inject [--to all|<pid>] [--isolate] [--dll <file>]
dotnet scion graft restore [--to all|<pid>]
dotnet scion graft disable <slot> [--to all|<pid>]
dotnet scion graft promote <Name> [--dry-run]
dotnet scion graft watch [--recipe <Id>]
```

## Description

Drafts live in `grafts.staging` (`scion/grafts/`); promoted grafts in `grafts.promoted`. All commands read the test
build for types and signatures; none starts Unity.

## graft new

Writes `scion/grafts/<Name>.cs`: namespace from the project, `using` lines, a `public static class <Name>` and a
method `Before` or `After` whose signature binds to the target, with `ref Call<T>` when it returns a value.

## graft check

Compiles the given files (default: every draft, and promoted grafts changed since the build) with the build's
assemblies, runs the analyzers and the weaver's rules (SCN101 to SCN113), and returns `diagnostics[]`. `--strict`
treats warnings as errors. `--hook` prints Claude Code hook JSON and only checks files under the grafts folders.

## graft build

Compiles drafts with the test defines against `Managed/*.dll`, generates the dispatchers the weaver would, and writes
`.scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_<hash>.dll` with the target `build_id` and ABI.

## graft inject

Sends the DLL (building first if drafts changed) to live copies of this build through the control channel. Default
merges by graft identity; `--isolate` runs only the DLL's grafts on the anchors it touches.

## graft restore

Every slot of the target copies back to the promoted grafts.

## graft disable

Empties one slot (promoted grafts included) in the target copies.

## graft promote

Moves `scion/grafts/<Name>.cs` to the promoted folder (`git mv` when tracked) and stages it. Rebuild to compile it
into the game.

## graft watch

On every save under the drafts folder: build, inject into all live copies, and, with `--recipe`, run it warm. Prints
one JSON line per cycle until Ctrl-C, then the summary.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--after`, `--before <Type.Method>` | new | The target and side. |
| `--strict` | check | Warnings fail. |
| `--hook` | check | Hook output for agents. |
| `--to all\|<pid>` | inject, restore, disable | Target copies (default all). |
| `--isolate` | inject | Replace instead of merge. |
| `--dll <file>` | inject | A DLL built elsewhere. |
| `--recipe <Id>` | watch | Run after each injection. |
| `--dry-run` | new, promote | Change nothing. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/graft-check -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"graft check","ok":false,"files":1,"diagnostics":[{"file":"scion/grafts/CritShake.cs","line":7,"code":"SCN103","message":"HitPresenter.Ply does not exist.","hint":"Did you mean 'Play'?","did_you_mean":["Play"]}],"errors":1,"warnings_count":0,"next_step":"fix scion/grafts/CritShake.cs:7, then: dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/CritShake.cs"}
```

Each command's fields are in its schema: `cli/graft-new`, `cli/graft-check`, `cli/graft-build`, `cli/graft-inject`,
`cli/graft-restore`, `cli/graft-disable`, `cli/graft-promote`, `cli/graft-watch` ([JSON Schemas](/scion/reference/schemas/)).

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done; `check` found no errors. |
| 1 | Diagnostics with errors; an injection with errors in some copy. |
| 2 | Bad option, unknown target or name. |
| 3 | No build, no live copies, a copy without `SCION_SLOTS`. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCN101`-`SCN113` | 1 | Graft rules. | [Graft diagnostics](/scion/reference/diagnostics/grafts/). |
| `SCN130`, `SCN131` | 1 | The DLL does not match the copy's build or ABI. | `graft build` again; same Scion version. |
| `no_copies` | 3 | No live copy. | `dotnet scion trial serve -j 2`. |
| `not_supported` | 3 | A copy built without `SCION_SLOTS`. | Use the test build. |
| `no_match` | 2 | Unknown target, draft or slot. | `did_you_mean`. |
| warning `recycle` | 0 | A copy passed 50 injections. | `trial serve` restarts it at the next boundary. |

## Examples

### The inner loop

```sh
dotnet scion graft new CritShake --after Orchard.Presentation.HitPresenter.Play
dotnet scion graft check scion/grafts/CritShake.cs
dotnet scion graft inject
dotnet scion trial run --warm SlashHit
```

### Strict check in CI

```sh
dotnet scion graft check --strict
```

## See also

- [From draft to final build](/scion/grafts/lifecycle/)
- [Live injection](/scion/grafts/injection/)
- [Hooks](/scion/agents/hooks/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# bisect

`dotnet scion bisect` runs `git bisect` between a good and a bad revision. At each step it builds the test player
cold, runs one recipe for some rounds and decides good, bad or skip, comparing on the hash, the images or one check.
It prints the first bad commit and a log of every step.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion bisect <Id> --good <rev> [--bad <rev>] [--on hash|pixels|check:<id>] [--rounds N]
```

## Description

1. Requires a clean working tree; records the starting branch to return to.
2. Runs the recipe at `--good` to record the reference (hash, images or check status).
3. `git bisect start <bad> <good>` and `git bisect run` with a step that builds, runs and compares.
4. Each step exits 0 (good), 1 (bad) or 125 (skip: the build failed, the id is missing, rounds disagree).
5. Returns to the starting branch and prints `first_bad`.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `<Id>` | required | The recipe id. |
| `--good <rev>` | required | A good revision. |
| `--bad <rev>` | `HEAD` | A bad revision. |
| `--on hash\|pixels\|check:<id>` | `hash` | What decides good or bad. |
| `--rounds N` | 2 | Rounds per step. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/bisect -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"bisect","ok":true,"id":"KnightFalls","good":"3f2a0b1","bad":"HEAD","on":"check:order","steps":4,"skipped":[],"first_bad":{"commit":"9d0c4e2","subject":"Play unit_down before the last hit number","date":"2026-10-10T11:05:00Z"},"log":".scion/bisect/20261012-140000/log.txt","next_step":"git show 9d0c4e2"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | `first_bad` found. |
| 1 | Too many skips: a range instead of one commit. |
| 2 | Dirty tree, bad revision, unknown id. |
| 3 | Build environment errors at the good revision. |
| 125 | Only from a single step, to `git bisect`: skip this commit. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `usage` | 2 | Uncommitted changes. | Commit or stash. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | A revision git does not know. | Check the revision. |
| `no_match` | 2 | The id does not exist at `--good`. | Pass `--recipes` with a DLL that has it. |
| `interrupted` | 3 | Ctrl-C. | The CLI resets `git bisect` and the branch. |

## Examples

### Pixels between releases

```sh
dotnet scion bisect SlashHit --good v1.3.0 --bad v1.4.0 --on pixels
```

### A probe check

```sh
dotnet scion bisect FireballArea --good 3f2a0b1 --on check:probe:damage
```

## See also

- [Bisect a regression](/scion/explore/bisect/)
- [Exit codes](/scion/reference/exit-codes/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# diagnose

`dotnet scion diagnose` reads the determinism scans the weaver writes when Unity compiles
(`Library/Scion/determinism-<assembly>.json`) and reports the adoption level, counts per SCN301 to SCN307, the
blockers with file and line, the singletons that block the mosaic, an ordered plan and, with `--adapter`, an adapter
skeleton for the game.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion diagnose [--assembly <name>]... [--adapter] [--dry-run]
```

## Description

Blockers are SCN303 to SCN307 findings in code that runs during recipes, and structural problems (no adapter, global
state). The plan orders them by how much they unlock. The full report goes to `Library/Scion/diagnose.md`.

With `--adapter`, `diagnose` writes `Assets/<Game>/Trials/GameAdapter.cs`: a `TrialAdapter<GameRecipe>` and a
`GameRecipe` base, with `Prepare`, `Run`, `Teardown` and `StateHash` stubs naming the game's scenes and the types it
found (`Battle`, `BattleState`).

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--assembly <name>` | every scanned assembly | Repeat to scan only some. |
| `--adapter` | off | Write the adapter skeleton. |
| `--dry-run` | off | With `--adapter`, print it instead. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/diagnose -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"diagnose","ok":true,"adoption_level":2,"assemblies":["Orchard.Core","Orchard.Runtime"],"counts":{"SCN301":14,"SCN302":2,"SCN303":1,"SCN304":0,"SCN305":0,"SCN306":0,"SCN307":0},"blockers":[{"file":"Assets/Orchard/Runtime/TurnTimer.cs","line":31,"code":"SCN303","message":"TurnTimer.Tick reads the wall clock (Stopwatch.GetTimestamp), which is not redirected."}],"singletons":[],"plan":["Use Time in TurnTimer.Tick or mark it [WallClock]."],"adapter_skeleton":null,"report":"Library/Scion/diagnose.md","next_step":"fix Assets/Orchard/Runtime/TurnTimer.cs:31, then: dotnet scion trial run --rounds 2 --check"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Reported (blockers do not fail). |
| 2 | Unknown assembly. |
| 3 | No scan files. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_match` | 2 | `--assembly` names an assembly without a scan. | `did_you_mean`. |
| `out_not_writable` | 3 | `Library/Scion/` cannot be written. | Check permissions. |
| warning `recipes_unchecked` | 0 | No scan yet. | Open the project in Unity once. |

## Examples

### Write the adapter skeleton

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose --adapter
```

### Only the core

```sh
dotnet scion diagnose --assembly Orchard.Core
```

## See also

- [Find non-determinism](/scion/determinism/diagnose/)
- [SCN301-SCN307](/scion/reference/diagnostics/determinism/)
- [Add Scion to an existing game](/scion/start/existing-project/)

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# index, guard

`dotnet scion index` prints a project index under 2 KB: the Scion version, the adoption level, the grafts folders,
anchor categories, recipes and the commands that matter, for an agent's session start. `dotnet scion guard` decides
whether an agent's action on baselines or generated files is allowed, needs a person, or is denied. Both have a
`--hook` mode that speaks Claude Code's hook format.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion index [--hook] [--write <file>]
dotnet scion guard [--approve] [--hook] [--path <file>] [--command "<cmd>"]
```

## Description

Both commands are fast (well under a second), read only local files and never start Unity, so agent hooks can call
them on every session and tool use.

## index

Builds the index from `scion.json`, the manifest (or the build) and the baselines. With `--write <file>`, keeps the
index and the agent rules between `<!-- scion:begin -->` and `<!-- scion:end -->` in `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`,
leaving the rest of the file alone. With `--hook`, wraps it as `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` for
`SessionStart`.

## guard

| Situation | Decision |
|---|---|
| An edit or write under `scion/baselines/` | `deny`: only `trial approve` writes baselines. |
| An edit of `scion.manifest.json` or `GRAFTS.md` | `deny`: generated by `gen`. |
| `trial approve` of ids that are only `new` | `allow`. |
| `trial approve` that would replace a baseline (`--approve`) | `ask`, with what changed and the review command. |
| Anything else | `allow`. |

With `--hook`, `guard` reads the hook input from stdin (tool name, path, command) and prints
`hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision`. Every hook finishes under one second and fails open, except the baselines
guard, which fails closed.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--hook` | both | Claude Code hook input and output. |
| `--write <file>` | index | Maintain the block in an instructions file. |
| `--approve` | guard | Check a `trial approve` command. |
| `--path <file>` | guard | Check an edit of this path (without `--hook`). |
| `--command "<cmd>"` | guard | Check this command (without `--hook`). |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/index -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"index","ok":true,"text":"This project uses Scion 1.0.0 (adoption level 3). Grafts: Assets/Orchard/Grafts (promoted), scion/grafts (drafts). Recipes: SlashHit, FireballArea, KnightFalls, CoopTurn (4 players), HudStates, UnitGallery. Approve only new baselines.","bytes":214,"block":null,"next_step":"none"}
```

<!-- validate: cli/guard -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"guard","ok":true,"decision":"ask","reason":"This approves SlashHit (changed: image) and replaces a baseline a person approved.","path":null,"approve":"SlashHit","next_step":"a person reviews: dotnet scion trial show SlashHit --grid"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Printed (a `deny` is still exit 0 in hook mode; the decision is in the JSON). |
| 2 | Bad option. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 0 in hook mode | Not a Scion project. | The hooks do nothing outside Scion projects. |
| `usage` | 2 | `guard` without `--hook`, `--path` or `--command`. | Pass one. |

## Examples

### Keep CLAUDE.md current

```sh
dotnet scion index --write CLAUDE.md
```

### Test the guard by hand

```sh
dotnet scion guard --command "dotnet scion trial approve --changed --reason x"
```

## See also

- [Hooks](/scion/agents/hooks/)
- [Project index and manifest](/scion/agents/project-index/)
- [Baselines and approval](/scion/trials/baselines/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# gen

`dotnet scion gen` reads the project's code and writes two generated files at the project root:
`scion.manifest.json` (every anchor, graft, tunable, recipe and probe, for tools and agents) and `GRAFTS.md` (the
same data as tables, for people and pull requests). `--list` prints one kind of item without writing. Run it after
changing attributes; CI checks the files are current.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion gen [--check] [--dry-run]
dotnet scion gen --list anchors|grafts|tunables|recipes|probes [--search <text>]
```

## Description

Sources, in order: the test build's DLLs (Mono.Cecil) when they are newer than the sources; otherwise the C# sources
(Roslyn). Output is sorted and stable, so the same code always gives the same bytes.

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` | off | Write nothing; exit 1 if the files are not current. |
| `--list <kind>` | | Print items of one kind. |
| `--search <text>` | | Filter `--list`. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Print what would change. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/gen -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"gen","ok":true,"manifest":"scion.manifest.json","grafts_md":"GRAFTS.md","anchors":26,"grafts":4,"tunables":9,"changed":true,"next_step":"git add scion.manifest.json GRAFTS.md"}
```

With `--list tunables`, `items[]` holds `key`, `type`, `min`, `max`, `value`, `layer` (`visual` or `rule`) and `doc`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Written, listed, or current. |
| 1 | `--check` and the files are out of date. |
| 2 | Unknown `--list` kind. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bad_value` | 2 | Unknown kind. | `anchors`, `grafts`, `tunables`, `recipes`, `probes`. |
| warning `name_at_run_time` | 0 | A target named by a computed string. | Use `nameof` or a literal. |

## Examples

### Check in CI

```sh
dotnet scion gen --check
```

### Every rule tunable

```sh
dotnet scion gen --list tunables --search Balance
```

## See also

- [Project index and manifest](/scion/agents/project-index/)
- [scion.manifest.json and GRAFTS.md](/scion/reference/files/manifest/)
- [Tunables and presets](/scion/grafts/tunables/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# judge

The `judge` commands manage the Scion Judge: `judge list` and `judge show` describe heads, `judge new` creates one
from a question file, `judge vote` opens a local page for blind duels and labels, `judge train` trains and promotes a
new head version, and `judge run` scores a run's captures. Heads, questions and votes live in `judge.dir`
(`scion/judge/`); embeddings in `judge.cache`.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion judge list
dotnet scion judge show <head>
dotnet scion judge new <head> --question <file> [--view full|hud|corners|actor] [--sequence]
dotnet scion judge vote [--run <run>] [--head <head>] [--synthetic N] [--gold <set> --count N] [--regold] [--top N]
dotnet scion judge train <head>
dotnet scion judge run <run> [--heads a,b] [--references N] [--pairs <run>]
```

## Description

The judge never changes a verdict or an exit code of trials. It runs locally with the eye model in `judge.eyes`.

## judge list

Every head with its version, type, vote count and gold agreement.

## judge show

One head: question, view, eyes, training history, calibration, and where it disagrees most with people.

## judge new

Creates `scion/judge/heads/<head>.json` from a question file. `--sequence` makes a motion head that also reads
`metrics.json`.

## judge vote

Starts a local page at `http://localhost:<port>/` and opens it. Pairs come from `--run` (or the latest runs), blind
and in both orders; the judge picks the most informative pairs first. `--synthetic N` adds N agent-made pairs
(degradations, fabricated bugs). `--gold <set> --count N` collects gold votes (people only). `--regold` re-asks a
sample of gold votes to measure the ceiling. `--top N` shows only the N best variants per id.

## judge train

Trains a new version with cross-validation and promotes it only if it agrees more with the gold set.

## judge run

Scores every capture of a run with the given heads (default: all), writes `<run>/judge.json` and `escalate`.
`--references N` adds the N most similar reference screens per capture; `--pairs <run>` compares each id with the
same id in another run.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--question <file>` | new | The question. |
| `--view <view>` | new | `full`, `hud`, `corners`, `actor`. |
| `--sequence` | new | A motion head. |
| `--run`, `--head` | vote | Where pairs come from; which head. |
| `--synthetic N`, `--gold <set>`, `--count N`, `--regold`, `--top N` | vote | See above. |
| `--heads a,b`, `--references N`, `--pairs <run>` | run | See above. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/judge -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"judge run","ok":true,"results":".scion/runs/20261011-150512/judge.json","escalate":["HudStates/turn-banner.720p.png"],"next_step":"look at the escalated captures, or ask an evaluator: dotnet scion trial eval 20261011-150512 --with agent"}
```

`judge list` returns `heads[]`; `judge show` and `judge train` return `head` (and `training`); `judge vote` returns
`url` and `votes`.

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done. |
| 2 | Unknown head, bad question file. |
| 3 | The eye model is missing. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model_missing` | 3 | The eye model is not downloaded. | Run the command in `hint` (also in `doctor --level 3`). |
| `no_match` | 2 | Unknown head. | `judge list`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | The question file does not validate. | Check it against `judge-question.schema.json`. |
| `not_supported` | 2 | `judge vote` without a browser (an agent). | Votes are for people; agents use `trial eval`. |

## Examples

### Score a run with two heads

```sh
dotnet scion judge run 20261011-150512 --heads readability,has_glitch
```

### Ten minutes of votes

```sh
dotnet scion judge vote --head hit_weight
```

## See also

- [The Judge](/scion/judge/overview/)
- [Train a head](/scion/judge/training/)
- [Judge data files](/scion/reference/files/judge-data/)

---

> Scion 1.0.0 documentation. Index of every page: https://jand-s.github.io/scion/41664431a8f5/llms.txt

# multiverse

`dotnet scion multiverse run` replays a captured match on the core simulator up to a turn, forks it, plays each
variant to the end and reports, per variant, whether the rules diverged, the first turn and the first field.
`dotnet scion multiverse show` prints a past result. With `--mosaic`, the test build replays the variants side by
side.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion multiverse run <match|Id> --at-turn <N> --variants <list|file> [--mosaic]
dotnet scion multiverse show <run>
```

## Description

Everything except `--mosaic` runs in plain .NET on the registered `ISimulation`, in parallel, without Unity.

## multiverse run

`<match>` is a captured match name (`knight-dies-to-crit`), its file, or a `CapturedMatch[...]` id. Variants: preset
names or blends, `tunable:<Key>=<value>`, `grafts:<dll>`, `bot:<name>`, comma-separated, or a JSON file with a list of
`{name, kind, value}`. Results go to `.scion/multiverse/<yyyyMMdd-HHmmss>/multiverse.json`.

## multiverse show

Prints the envelope of a past run from its `multiverse.json`.

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--at-turn <N>` | run | Fork after turn N (0 = the start). |
| `--variants <list\|file>` | run | The variants. |
| `--mosaic` | run | Also replay in the test build and write `mosaic.png`. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/multiverse -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"multiverse show","ok":true,"run":"/Users/alex/orchard/.scion/multiverse/20261012-101500","match":"knight-dies-to-crit","at_turn":2,"variants":[{"name":"base","diverged":false,"first_turn":null,"field":null},{"name":"crit-1200","diverged":true,"first_turn":3,"field":"units[0].hp"}],"report":"multiverse.json","mosaic":"mosaic.png","next_step":"open mosaic.png"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done. Divergence of tunable or preset variants is information, not failure. |
| 1 | A `grafts:` variant diverged (grafts must be visual). |
| 2 | Unknown match, variant or turn. |
| 3 | No simulation, or the state cannot be saved. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | No `[assembly: Simulation]`. | Register an `ISimulation`. |
| `not_forkable` | 3 | No `ISaveable`. | Implement `Save` and `Load`. |
| `mosaic_unsupported` | 3 | `--mosaic` without `IMosaicAdapter`. | Implement it or drop `--mosaic`. |
| `no_match` | 2 | Unknown match or preset. | `trial list`; `scion/presets/`. |

## Examples

### Prove a draft is visual

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 0 --variants base,grafts:.scion/grafts/ScionGrafts_51c2.dll
```

### See variants side by side

```sh
dotnet scion multiverse run knight-dies-to-crit --at-turn 2 --variants base,heavy --mosaic
```

## See also

- [The multiverse](/scion/explore/multiverse/)
- [Turn any match into a recipe](/scion/trials/captured-matches/)
- [Mosaic](/scion/trials/mosaic/)

# hunt, search

Two exploration commands. `dotnet scion hunt run` plays matches on the core simulator with mutated commands, keeps
those that reach new features and saves each find as a match in `scion/recipes/found/`. `dotnet scion search run`
explores tunables with paired Bayesian optimization, keeps a MAP-Elites gallery, filters with the spec and the judge
and asks a person the deciding duels.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion hunt run <Id|Spec> [--budget <minutes>] [--seed <n>] [--save]
dotnet scion search run <Spec> [--tunables a,b] [--budget <n>] [--duels <n>] [--niches a,b]
```

## Description

Both are long-running: they report progress, stop cleanly on Ctrl-C and keep what they found so far.

## hunt run

Runs for `--budget` minutes (default 5) on the `ISimulation`, from the recipe's setup or the spec's balance setup.
Each new feature reported by `ISimulation.Features` produces one find, minimized to the fewest turns. Finds go to
`scion/recipes/found/<feature>-<n>.match.json` with `source: hunt`.

## search run

Evaluates `--budget` variants (default 40) of the selected tunables as recipe variants in the test build (or on the
simulator for balance-only specs), drops those failing the spec, ranks with the judge, keeps the best per niche in
`search.json`, and asks up to `--duels` blind duels (default 10).

## Options

| Option | Commands | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--budget` | both | Minutes (hunt) or variants (search). |
| `--seed <n>` | hunt | Repeatable hunts. |
| `--save` | hunt | Save finds (default on; `--save false` to only report). |
| `--tunables a,b` | search | What to tune. |
| `--duels <n>` | search | Maximum duels for a person (0 = none). |
| `--niches a,b` | search | Metrics that define the gallery's niches. |

## Output

<!-- validate: cli/hunt-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"hunt run","ok":true,"target":"CoopTurn","budget_s":300,"states":91540,"features":33,"finds":[{"name":"multi_kill-0003","file":"scion/recipes/found/multi_kill-0003.match.json","feature":"multi_kill"}],"next_step":"dotnet scion trial run \"CapturedMatch[match=multi_kill-0003]\""}
```

<!-- validate: cli/search-run -->
```json
{"schema_version":1,"command":"search run","ok":true,"spec":"StrongerCrits","tunables":["CritShake.Strength","CritShake.Stop"],"evaluated":40,"duels":8,"gallery":".scion/search/20261012-120000/search.json","best":[{"name":"g03","values":{"CritShake.Strength":0.55,"CritShake.Stop":0.07},"score":0.79}],"next_step":"save g03 as a preset in scion/presets/"}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | Done (no finds is still 0). |
| 2 | Unknown target, spec or tunable. |
| 3 | No simulation; judge model missing. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `no_simulation` | 3 | No `ISimulation`. | Register one. |
| `model_missing` | 3 | The spec uses a judge head and the eyes are missing. | `doctor --level 3`. |
| `bad_value` | 2 | A tunable without a range. | `[Tunable(min, max)]`. |
| `no_match` | 2 | Unknown spec or recipe. | `did_you_mean`. |

## Examples

### A ten-minute hunt

```sh
dotnet scion hunt run CoopTurn --budget 10
```

### A search without people

```sh
dotnet scion search run StrongerCrits --tunables CritShake.Strength,CritShake.Stop --duels 0
```

## See also

- [Rare-moment hunter](/scion/explore/rare-moments/)
- [Guided search](/scion/explore/guided-search/)
- [Turn any match into a recipe](/scion/trials/captured-matches/)

# mcp

`dotnet scion mcp` starts a Model Context Protocol server on stdin and stdout. Agents that speak MCP call Scion's
commands as tools (`scion_<noun>_<verb>`, with the same arguments and the same JSON envelope as structured content)
and read the documentation of the installed version with `docs_search` and `docs_read`. The server is started by the
agent's client, not by you.

## Synopsis

```text
dotnet scion mcp [--root <path>] [--log <file>]
```

## Description

The server implements MCP over stdio: `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, progress notifications and
cancellation. Every tool runs the corresponding command in-process from the project root and returns its envelope as
`structuredContent`, with `isError` true for exit codes 2 and 3. Commands that need a person or never end have no
tool. The full tool list is on [MCP server](/scion/agents/mcp/).

## Options

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--root <path>` | the nearest `scion.json` from the working directory | The project root. |
| `--log <file>` | none | Write a log of requests (never to stdout). |

## Output

The server writes only MCP messages to stdout. A `tools/call` result:

```json
{"structuredContent":{"schema_version":1,"command":"anchor list","ok":true,"total":26,"anchors":[],"next_step":"dotnet scion anchor show presentation.hit"},"isError":false}
```

## Exit codes

| Code | When |
|---|---|
| 0 | The client closed stdin. |
| 2 | Bad option. |
| 3 | No project root. |

## Errors

| Code | Exit | Cause | Next action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `config_not_found` | 3 | No `scion.json` from the working directory or `--root`. | Set `--root` in the client config. |
| `busy` | tool error | Another long command is running. | The server queues calls; wait for the first. |

## Examples

### Claude Code project config

```json
{"mcpServers":{"scion":{"command":"dotnet","args":["scion","mcp"]}}}
```

### Debug with a log

```sh
dotnet scion mcp --log /tmp/scion-mcp.log
```

## See also

- [MCP server](/scion/agents/mcp/)
- [Set up your agent](/scion/agents/setup/)
